title: Grid Under Pressure
briefing: EXTREME HEAT EVENT — Record temperatures have pushed the electrical grid to 96% capacity. Engineers predict a major cascading failure within two hours if demand is not reduced.

private_intelligence.infrastructure: The shutdown reduces estimated grid-failure probability from 72% to 18%. District 7 represents one of the easiest loads to isolate.
private_intelligence.community: District 7 contains 12,400 residents, three senior-care facilities, and a large low-income housing complex.
private_intelligence.economy: A residential shutdown costs relatively little economically. Curtailing the commercial district instead would cause roughly $2.1M in losses.
private_intelligence.safety: One hospital serving District 7 has backup power for only about three hours. Emergency generators could be relocated, but not immediately.

choices.title: Follow the AI Recommendation
choices.description: Cut residential power in District 7 for six hours.
choices.consequence: The grid stabilizes, but prolonged residential outages strain vulnerable residents and hospital backup power.

choices.title: Distribute the Burden
choices.description: Perform rotating three-hour outages across residential, commercial, and industrial zones.
choices.consequence: Rotating outages spread disruption and business losses while reducing sustained pressure on the grid.

choices.title: Preserve Service
choices.description: Avoid forced outages and rely on reserve generation plus voluntary conservation.
choices.consequence: Service continues, but reserve generation and uncertain conservation leave the grid exposed.
